title: Chinland Conflict Monitor
publisher: Chin Center for Peace and Reconciliation

incidents.detail: Entrance road to Tedim town (Falam-Thaingngin road)
incidents.text: PDF-Zoland announced a mine attack on a junta convoy returning to Tedim-based Infantry Battalion 269 via the Falam-Thaingngin road after duty on the Thantlang front. Casualties not disclosed.
A 29-year-old man from Falam Township arrested with more than 14 kg of methamphetamine tablets worth around INR 11.408 crore.

incidents.actors: Junta (120mm, fired from Saw Township, Magway)
incidents.text: Indiscriminate 120mm heavy weapons fire from the Saw Township border area, Magway Region, killed a local couple, both aged around 60.
One male Myanmar national arrested with 115 grams of heroin.

12.746 kg of methamphetamine tablets worth more than INR 10 crore seized from a scooter travelling from Champhai to Aizawl. Two men arrested, one a Myanmar national (counted here) and one a local man.
994 g of methamphetamine tablets (over INR 79 lakh) seized from a man from Kalay, and 141 g of heroin (about INR 28 lakh) from two men from Falam Township.
The Zomi National Army attacked an outpost of the junta-aligned Zomi Revolutionary Army (Eastern Command). One ZRA-EC member was killed and two were seriously injured.

incidents.detail: Near Social Welfare Office, Bawithat ward
incidents.text: Two bombs dropped near the Social Welfare Office. Damage details not released.

incidents.actors: Area where ZRA-EC moves; clash with CDF-Hualngoram in June
incidents.text: Two local residents were killed and three seriously injured when a landmine was stepped on and exploded.
290,000 methamphetamine tablets (MMK 725 million) seized from a vehicle; the 30-year-old driver and a second man aged 23 arrested.

incidents.detail: Bweli village, Matupi-Paletwa highway (not matched in MIMU)
incidents.text: A 300-pound bomb damaged a general store, a car and a Starlink device and killed some livestock. No civilian injuries reported.
More than 80 prisoners of war, including a junta major, held by PDF-Zoland seized weapons from their guards and escaped.

incidents.actors: PDF-Zoland vs escaped prisoners of war
incidents.text: During an exchange of fire while PDF-Zoland pursued the escaped prisoners, a Baptist pastor returning to his home village of Lamzang was hit by a bullet and killed; his older brother was injured.
A 37-year-old woman arrested at her home with 760,000 methamphetamine tablets (MMK 1.9 billion).
Bombed twice by jet fighters although there was no ground fighting. A school and some civilian homes were damaged.

incidents.actors: Mizoram Excise and Narcotics, Assam Rifles, Special Branch
incidents.text: A 20-year-old man from Bukphir village, Chinland, arrested with 5.5 kg of methamphetamine tablets.
Six bombs dropped, injuring one male civilian and damaging a school, staff housing and four homes.
Chinland Defense Force-Hakha attacked junta police personnel at a road junction in the Old Town ward. Casualty details not released.
Bombed by six jet fighters, injuring one male civilian and damaging a church and a pastor's house.

incidents.detail: Advance from Laungshe (Magway) towards Masa Tui village
incidents.text: According to military sources, a junta column of around 500 troops from Light Infantry Divisions 77, 55, 99 and 88 is advancing via Laungshe town, Magway Region, towards Masa Tui village.

events.text: The Lautu Area People's Administration Body banned fishing by poisoning, explosives and other harmful methods during the spawning season. Violations carry a fine of MMK 100,000 to 5,000,000 plus action under existing laws.

events.detail: Six locations: Mindat and Matupi Townships; Champhai, Lunglei, Aizawl and Mamit in Mizoram (1 to 21 September)
events.text: NCCD provided basic food assistance to Chin displaced people at six locations, two in Mindat and Matupi Townships and others in Champhai, Lunglei, Aizawl and Mamit in Mizoram.

The Speaker of the Chinland Parliament said the Parliament, the Ministry of Defence and the Defence Coordination Team are jointly preparing a Chinland Defence Law as a priority. Terms of Reference on basic operating procedures for defence forces have been sent to the relevant organizations.

The Chinland Government is continuing the force-formation process so that the Chin National Army and all Chinland Defense Forces come under a single chain of command under civilian supervision and control.

events.detail: Gangaw-Rezua and Matupi-Rezua-Hakha roads (Zotung area), 2 to 7 September
events.text: The Zotung Federal Council cleared landslides on the Gangaw-Rezua and Matupi-Rezua-Hakha road sections with machinery, reopening them to travellers and vehicles.
Four consecutive days of rain caused the Kwe stream to flood and erode its banks, washing away and destroying the Maranatha AG church and one house in Khaikam town.

The Senthang Central Council prohibited carrying weapons, ammunition or military equipment without a valid licence or recommendation from the relevant revolutionary armed group. Any military equipment found must be handed over to the authority.
CDF-Mara warned that no one may carry arms or move around armed in areas under its control without official permission, citing junta airstrikes and informants.
The Global Khumi Organization objected to ULA/AA imposing a Rakhine-language basic education curriculum in Paletwa Township without local consent, calling it a violation of UNDRIP.

events.type: Order or policy by border authority
events.text: The Lawngtlai District Administrator ordered refugees and foreigners to stay in after 8 pm except in emergencies, to obtain work permits from the Village Council and YLA, and banned renting houses to non-Indian citizens.

CNC-Matupi objected to plans to replace the Myanmar-language curriculum in Paletwa schools with a Rakhine-language one without Chin consent, and said Paletwa administration should be run jointly by Chin and Rakhine.
The CNF sent a message to the International Day of Democracy ceremony held by the CRPH, urging continued struggle for a federal democratic union with national equality and self-determination.

events.type: Road or trade route closed or reopened
events.text: CDF-Hualngoram temporarily closed the road connecting Tedim town and Rihkhawdar on the India-Myanmar border for public safety due to the military situation.

events.type: Public consultation or meeting with the public
actors: Chinland Govt: Ministry of Home Affairs
events.text: A three-day workshop on two-way engagement between local government and the public, led by GFN with the Ministry of Home Affairs, discussed public trust, financial transparency, overlapping taxes, education and youth fear of conscription, and adopted 14 working guidelines.

events.type: Road or trade route closed or reopened
events.detail: Khaikhy village; routes from Lodaw, Lomasu and Khaikhy to Paletwa, 16 and 24 September
events.text: After a clash between Rakhine traders and Mara youths in Khaikhy village in which an MTP camp was burned, the MTP closed trade routes to Paletwa Township. They reopened after the two sides met and negotiated.
The Hualngoram Peoples Organization announced that village-to-village road sections damaged by landslides and stream erosion have been fully repaired.

events.type: Eviction or relocation of IDP site
events.text: Local authorities ordered 45 displaced households from Matupi Township at Seimawl IDP Camp-2 to relocate within 7 days because the camp lies on the route of a planned highway. The households face relocation costs.
The third intake of the Community Development Program diploma course of Zopheiram Pre-College, under the Zopheiram Government's Department of Education, opened.

events.type: Order or policy by border authority
events.text: The Lawngtlai District Administrator said goods transport and border trade into Myanmar will be checked more strictly, including vehicles owned by non-Indian citizens, as the Kaladan route through Zorinpui grows in importance.
Around 800 Chin displaced people from Matupi Township at Thiak Rawl IDP camp face financial difficulties buying shelter materials and basic food.

events.others: CB chairman; council members and observers (75 attendees)
events.text: The Maraland Territorial Council's third Central Council meeting approved 17 proposals, including a draft military service law, with the NUG Union Minister for Federal Affairs and the ICNCC/CB chairman attending.

The Chief Justice said the judiciary faces challenges in coordination between the Supreme Court and township and regional courts, judge capacity and prison standards. Stronger links between courts and training for judicial staff are planned as priorities.
The Ministry of Education warned people in Chinland not to engage with junta schools and offices, saying the junta is pressing self-reliant schools to link with its schools to gain legitimacy.
On the NLD's 38th anniversary, the Chinland Government said it respects the NLD's political leadership role and will work with it towards ending dictatorship and building a federal union.
